paper_metadata.title: High Gain–Bandwidth Differential Distributed InP D-HBT Driver Amplifiers With Large (11.3 Vpp) Output Swing at 40 Gb/s
paper_metadata.abstract: High-performance and compact 40-Gb/s driver amplifiers were realized in 1.2m emitter double-heterojunction InGaAs–InP HBT (D-HBT) technology with a maximum cut-off frequency ( ) of 150 GHz and a maximum oscillation frequency ( max) of 200 GHz. Two-stage differential drivers feature a lumped input and fully distributed output stage and deliver a maximum differential output swing of 11.3 V peak-to-peak ( pp) at 40 Gb/s with less then 350 fs of added rms jitter and rise and fall times of about 7 ps while consuming a total power of 3 W. When biased at a lower output swing of 6.3 pp, excellent 40-Gb/s eyes with a 7-ps fall time, 6-ps rise time, and no observable jitter deterioration compared with the input source are obtained at a reduced power consumption of 1.7 W. On-wafer measured differential -parameters show a differential gain of 25 dB, 50 GHz bandwidth, and input 20 dB from 2 to 45 GHz. The ampliand output reflection below fiers’ small die size (1.0 1.7 mm), relatively low power consumption, large output swing, and ability to have dc coupled inputs and outputs enable compact 40-Gb/s optical transmitters with good eye opening for both conventional transmission formats such as nonreturn-to-zero and return-to-zero and alternative formats such as duobinary and differential phase shift keying.
